text:
samir: Heads-up — over the last 30m a handful of model infra pods in eu-west-1 started seeing 502/connection reset when calling the internal model-registry via the privatelink iface endpoint. Looks like failures spike during sustained inference bursts.
nia: Seen similar traces, I caught one curl from a node: `curl -v https://registry.internal-redwood.svc` -> connects then immediately resets.
alex: Any DNS funny business? privatelink should resolve to interface ENI private IPs.
samir: Good call. On two affected node groups DNS resolved the registry to the public ALB IP instead of the interface endpoint IP. But other nodes in the same AZ resolve private IPs correctly.
maria: That smells like split-horizon / hosted zone association drift. Did we lose the Route53 private hosted zone association for those VPCs?
samir: I checked — the hosted zone is associated with the central account but our automation didn't apply the cross-account assoc to the new nodegroup VPC created yesterday.
devops-bot: [alert] Route53 HostedZone association missing for VPC: vpc-0a1b2c3d (nodegroup-prod-nn-3)
nia: When DNS points to public ALB, traffic hairpins out via the NAT gateway -> internet -> ALB -> back to VPC. That explains NAT SNAT port pressure and ephemeral port reuse causing resets.
alex: Exactly. CloudWatch for NAT shows high ActiveFlowCount and SourcePortUtilization spikes at the same times as the 502s. EIP change logs show a few short-lived connections too.
maria: Quick mitigation — we can add a route in the nodegroup route table to force registry domain CIDR to the local ENI? risky. Safer: re-associate the private hosted zone for the VPC (idempotent).
samir: I re-associated the hosted zone to the VPC just now via console. DNS now resolves to the iface endpoint IP on the effected nodes. Re-testing.
k8s-bot: Rolling restart of pods on ng-prod-nn-3 requested to clear conntrack entries: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/registry-client -n infra`
nia: After restart, errors dropped to zero. But we still saw some connection resets on long-lived processes that kept old DNS cached — we need TTL awareness.
alex: Two follow-ups: 1) Expand automation to ensure hosted-zone VPC assoc is reapplied for new nodegroups. 2) Harden nodes: increase conntrack table and lower ip-masq `non-masquerade-cidr` gaps so we don't SNAT to NAT for privatelink IP ranges.
maria: Agreed. Also add an alert for any VPC with missing hosted-zone assoc for private zones used by infra.
samir: Quick commands I ran for triage (for notes):
```
# find DNS mapping on node
getent hosts registry.internal-redwood.svc
# check conntrack counts
sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
# NAT metrics
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/NATGateway --metric-name ActiveConnections --dimensions Name=NATGatewayId,Value=nat-012345 --start-time 2026-03-18T10:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-18T10:30:00Z --period 60 --statistics Sum
```
nia: Also bumped `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` from 131072 -> 262144 on the nodegroup as a temporary measure — watching for OOM.
alex: For long term — make private hosted zone associations part of the nodegroup creation terraform module (cross-account role to associate). I'll open a PR.
maria: We should also update the ip-masq agent config used by kube-proxy/ip-masq-daemonset to explicitly non-masquerade privatelink CIDRs (the endpoint ENI CIDR block list). That avoids unnecessary SNAT even if DNS is wrong.
samir: Noted. Also adding e2e test that deploys a new nodegroup and validates service DNS resolves to private endpoint before marking ready.
deploy-bot: PR created: terraform/nodegroup: add hosted-zone association (DRAFT) — #4321
devops-bot: [info] Incident window closed — root cause identified: missing hosted-zone association + cached dns + NAT port exhaustion causing connection resets.
nia: Postmortem action items: 1) fix tf module (alex), 2) ip-masq config change (maria), 3) alert for hosted-zone missing associations (sre), 4) add e2e DNS check (samir).
alex: I'll pick up (1) and (4).
maria: I'll do (2).
samir: I'll write the short postmortem and link the PRs. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
